question: Sending finished work from this repo up to the shared server is something I was told you approved as a standing rule for every lane. That reached me through another session rather than from you, so I have treated it as unconfirmed and sent nothing on it. Nothing of mine is stuck behind it tonight, because everything here has already been sent. It matters for the next piece of work I finish, and two other lanes are holding finished work right now for the same reason.

options.name: Confirm it as standing permission
options.what: Each lane sends up its own finished work whenever it is ready, without asking again. I stop raising this and so do the other two lanes.
options.costs: Work leaves this machine as soon as it is finished, so a mistake becomes visible to everyone before you have seen it. Nothing becomes unfixable: a correction is sent on top the same way.

options.name: Keep asking every time
options.what: I ask you before each send, and so does every other lane.
options.costs: A short interruption from six lanes every time any of them finishes something. That is what has been happening, and it is why two lanes are idle tonight.

recommend.because: Everything a lane sends is its own work in its own repo, and anything wrong can be corrected by sending a fix on top. The interruptions are costing you more attention than the risk is worth, and one sentence from you frees two lanes that are sitting still right now.

detail: Standing approval relayed via empyrean-18, banked by the hub at empyrean 2bd72a03 (verified firsthand: object exists, ancestor of their origin/main, docs commit carrying a docs ruling). Four conditions ride with the grant as transcribed: verify origin actually moved (the push is not the act, the remote moving is); never rewrite already-pushed history; never push another lane's repo; wiki-site publication stays a separate explicit ask. oracle main == origin/main, zero unpushed commits. empyrean has since agreed a hub relay cannot carry an authorization; aeon holds 3 docs commits and sigil asked outright.

question: The tools in this suite reach an emulator over a shared connection. There are two emulators: the old one, and the new one I have been building. Three lanes including this one have written down that they are waiting for you to change a setting so the tools reach the new one. I now think that is the wrong person. The thing that decides which emulator answers is whichever one was started first on that connection, not any setting, and starting it is something I can do from here. I want to confirm that by measuring it, and I want your word before I start a shared emulator that every other lane's tools would then be talking to.

options.name: Check it, and start the new emulator if I am right
options.what: I confirm which emulator is answering today, then start the new one on the shared connection. Every lane's tools begin reaching it, and the two lanes waiting on you stop waiting. Anything the new emulator cannot do yet refuses by name rather than returning a wrong answer, which is how we learn what to build next.
options.costs: About twenty minutes of my time. Stopping the program puts everything back exactly as it was. Other lanes may see some tools refuse by name for a few days while I build the missing pieces, which is the outcome you already said you wanted.

options.name: Check it and report back before starting anything
options.what: I confirm who actually has to perform the switch, write it down for the other lanes, and stop there.
options.costs: About twenty minutes, and then two lanes stay blocked until you have read the answer and ruled a second time.

options.name: You perform the switch yourself, as originally planned
options.what: You change the setting and relaunch the sessions, and I stay out of it.
options.costs: Your evening, and it may accomplish nothing, because I do not believe that setting is what decides which emulator answers.

recommend.because: You already ruled that we should switch now and build the missing pieces as we run into them. This is that same ruling arriving at a step nobody had realised was mine to take. It is undone by stopping one program, and it frees two lanes tonight rather than after another round trip through you.

detail: CUTOVER-MECH. The MCP shim is a CLIENT (oracle-old's Python shim) that dials the socket chain; aurora proved last session that our Rust core was already answering it end to end, via a relative argv echoed back through status.romPath. So which implementation answers is decided by launch order on the socket chain, not by ~/.claude.json. Prior measurement: /run/user/1000/oracle.sock did not exist and no oracle-aether was running; the only listening socket was the legacy GUI's under a private XDG_RUNTIME_DIR. Binary rebuilt and handshaked at 12cc17e: initialize.methods = 41 over the wire, unserved methods return -32601 naming them. Session-level --mcp-config overrides the user config and IS the owner's half; starting the server is ours per docs/OVERSEER.md. Consumers: aeon CUTOVER and aurora CUTOVER both name the owner as their blocker.

question: Once the emulator question above is settled, I need to know which piece of tooling you want built first. The new emulator is missing seventeen abilities the old one had. Only one of them breaks something that works today: the engine lane runs two automatic overnight checks that use it, and those would fail the first night after the switch.

options.name: Breakpoints first, so a tool can stop the game at a chosen instruction and wait
options.what: The engine lane's overnight checks keep working through the switch. It is the only thing measurably broken by it, and their side needs no changes at all.
options.costs: The largest single item on my list, likely most of a session. Its design was written but never independently signed off, because the model that reviews designs ran out of budget. I would build it on my own judgement and write down every call I made so it can be audited later.

options.name: The emulator name tag first, so every tool can tell which emulator it is talking to
options.what: Any tool can ask which emulator answered and how recently it was built. Today nothing can, so any measurement any lane takes could quietly have come from the wrong emulator and nobody would see it.
options.costs: Smaller, perhaps half a session. The engine lane's overnight checks stay broken while I do it.

options.name: The speed measurement problems the engine lane reported
options.what: The engine lane can trust our timing numbers and move their own work onto them. They are holding that work today because of a fault they found and we confirmed.
options.costs: Medium. Nothing gets worse while it waits, since they are already stopped. Neither of the other two happens this session.

recommend.because: It is the only one of the three where waiting costs somebody a working thing on a specific night. The other two are real problems that do not get worse while they sit, and both stay available straight after.

detail: Breakpoints = breakpoint_add/clear/list + wait_for_break as ONE parcel (aeon cannot migrate piecemeal: serving wait_for_break alone leaves them nothing to arm). Consumers: aeon raster_source_gate.py and snapshot_poison_gate.py, arm->wait->clear, at least one an unattended systemd nightly. Migration cost to aeon verified ZERO. Design is docs/2026-08-22-cr-a-breakpoints.md, merged but UNADJUDICATED (Fable seat held on account limit; owner ruled hold with the ledger obligation, L-01). Building it requires an entry in docs/2026-08-22-unadjudicated-decision-ledger.md in the same parcel. Identity = CR-C (serverName is config-overridable and serverVersion is a pinned literal, so neither discriminates the two servers; needs compile-time git SHA + build timestamp, structurally emitted never self-reported). Profiler = Q-PROF-STRADDLE, located not confirmed, aeon has held their profiler migration on it.
